[8] (source: tradingqna; context: How to convert Coin SIP to Coin AMC SIP)
@Bhuvan Consider this case:-
 I am investing in Fund X through Coin as SIP, which is technically a lump-sum.
 At AMC level, Fund X is currently accepting both lump-sum and SIP. Thus I am able to invest through Coin.
 Suddenly, the AMC stops accepting fresh lump-sum and SIP mode both for Fund X. (e.g. SBI Small cap has done it in past). Only those who are already invested in SIP can continue their SIP.
 I won’t be able to continue my investment in Fund X through Coin because lump-sum mode is closed by AMC.
 Coin will react to this change and take some time to open the AMC-SIP mode, but remember AMC has already stopped accepting fresh SIP for Fund X.
 So essentially, I won’t be able to invest in Fund X anymore until AMC reopens it.

It’s as simple of this. If a fund stops accepting lumpsum investment, we’ll open up the AMC SIP mode of investing. You will just have ti restart the SIP.

[10] (source: tradingqna; context: How to convert Coin SIP to Coin AMC SIP)
If this happens, which it very rarely does, then yes, you won’t be able to invest. This has so far happened only in the case of a couple of smallcap funds.
 But the alternative is that you also have an option of investing in an alternative small-cap fund. With the new SEBI reclassification norms, the universe of stocks available for the fund managers to pick from is tightly defined. So, over a period of time, you will see that the return profiles of these stocks will be similar.
 Doesn’t take much time for us to do this. If a fund stops fresh lumpsum inflows, the new mode SIP will be available on the next day itself.
